## Overview

Adds `CanaryForConditionalGeneration` for [`nvidia/canary-1b-v2`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/canary-1b-v2) (FastConformer encoder + Transformer decoder; 25 European languages, ASR + X↔En speech translation). It targets the native Transformers checkpoint layout (`model_type: canary`, available since Transformers 5.16, which vLLM already pins), so no `.nemo` conversion or `trust_remote_code` is needed.

A user asked on the vLLM Slack whether `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` could work. No existing issue or PR: `gh pr list --search canary` / `gh issue list --search canary` only return unrelated NIXL "import canary" CI items.

The decoder is built from vLLM layers; the FastConformer encoder reuses the Transformers module, as `parakeet.py` already does (see Details).

## Claims

- `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` loads and serves via `LLM` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions` + `/v1/audio/translations` (source language from `language`, target from `to_language`, default `en` for translations).
- Greedy output is token-identical to Transformers `CanaryForConditionalGeneration.generate` on the clips below (fp32 and bf16, batched).
- WER on the existing `test_wer_correctness` earnings22 slice: 12.34 (vLLM, bf16, CPU) and 12.336 (vLLM, bf16, L40 GPU, unmodified test) vs 12.46 (Transformers, fp32); 12.34 is added as the expected value for `nvidia/canary-1b-v2`.

## Validation

The runs below are on an Apple M5 Pro (vLLM CPU backend, `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=2`). GPU results are in the next section.

**Token parity vs Transformers** (3 prompts in one `llm.generate` batch, greedy, `max_tokens=128`):

| clip | task | fp32 | bf16 | output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| en (6 s, TTS) | en→en | match | match | `The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Speech recognition on VLLM is now working.` |
| de (5 s, TTS) | de→de | match | match | `Guten Morgen, heute ist das Wetter sehr schön und wir gehen in den Park.` |
| de (5 s, TTS) | de→en | match | match | `Good morning, today is the weather very nice and we go into the park.` |

**WER** (`D4nt3/esb-datasets-earnings22-validation-tiny-filtered`, 511 clips, Whisper `EnglishTextNormalizer`, same code path as `test_wer_correctness`):

| implementation | dtype | WER |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transformers `generate` (greedy) | fp32 | 12.46 |
| vLLM (this PR), `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | bf16 | 12.34 |

The vLLM number came from calling the test's `run_evaluation` with `max_concurrent_reqs=8`; the unmodified test sends all 511 requests at once, which times out on CPU. The expected value was measured with bf16 on CPU; the test allows up to 12.56. On GPU the unmodified test passes with 12.336 (see below).

**Server checks** (`vllm serve nvidia/canary-1b-v2`):
- 67 s clip → chunked by the STT chunker (40 s limit) and transcribed correctly.
- 8 concurrent requests → identical outputs.
- `language=ja` → HTTP 400 with the supported-language list (see Details).

**Tests**

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_canary.py                     # 6 passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k canary  # 3 passed
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k Canary                      # passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                              # passed
```

`tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Canary` segfaults on macOS in the forked child (Whisper and Cohere ASR fail the same way there); on Linux it passes (below).

**GPU (single NVIDIA L40, Linux)**

- `test_wer_correctness[...-model_config2]` unmodified, all 511 requests at once: WER **12.336**, passed.
- `test_canary.py` (6), Canary's `processing/test_common.py` cases (3), `test_registry_imports[CanaryForConditionalGeneration]` and `test_can_initialize_large_subset[CanaryForConditionalGeneration]` pass.
- End-to-end through `vllm serve`: with `--dtype float32` the output text is identical to Transformers greedy on all 14 en/de transcription and de→en/en→de translation cases (in bf16, 2 near-tie cases differ by a word; see the linked comment). Long audio (79 s / 135 s) is chunked correctly, German WER is 8.0% on 4 MLS clips, `ja` returns 400, streaming matches non-streaming, and 16 concurrent requests match sequential ones. Details: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64215#issuecomment-6472494788
- CUDA graphs work. Throughput vs `whisper-large-v3` with `vllm bench serve` on the earnings22 slice: 43.8 vs 17.3 req/s at concurrency 32 and 59.1 vs 17.1 at 128. Details: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64215#issuecomment-6472054652

## Details

- **Decoder** is native vLLM: reuses `CohereASRAttention` / `CohereASRCrossAttention` / `CohereASRMLP` from `cohere_asr.py` (Transformers' Canary is itself a subclass of its Cohere ASR model). Differences from Cohere ASR: `[sin | cos]` positional table (vs interleaved), no encoder→decoder projection, `proj_out` with bias. Weight renames are decoder-scoped regexes in `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
- **Encoder** currently reuses Transformers' `ParakeetEncoder` as-is, the same way `parakeet.py` does for Nano Nemotron VL. Checkpoint names match 1:1, so correctness comes from the reference implementation. I'm keeping it this way in this PR: no ASR encoder in vLLM uses tensor-parallel layers yet (`cohere_asr.ConformerEncoder` also uses plain `nn.Linear`), so swapping in the Cohere ASR encoder would remove duplicated code without a TP or kernel benefit, and the model fits on one GPU. Sharing `cohere_asr.ConformerEncoder`, which needs a config adapter because it reads NeMo-style config dicts, could be a follow-up if reviewers prefer.
- **Processor**: `CanaryProcessor` renames `input_ids` → `decoder_input_ids`, so `_call_hf_processor` calls `ParakeetFeatureExtractor` and the tokenizer directly. Features are extracted per clip and passed with `feature_lengths`; the encoder mask is rebuilt after padding.
- **Prompt**: the same control-token sequence as the checkpoint's `chat_template.jinja` (`<|startofcontext|><|startoftranscript|><|emo:undefined|><|src|><|tgt|><|pnc|><|noitn|><|notimestamp|><|nodiarize|>`).
- **Languages**: `validate_language` rejects languages outside the 25 trained ones instead of the base class's warn-and-continue, because the prompt needs a trained language token; with `ja` the model silently returned empty text.
- **Limitations / TODO**: `max_audio_clip_s=40` is my choice for vLLM's chunker (NeMo uses its own dynamic chunking for long-form); no timestamps/ITN/diarization control tokens exposed yet (always `noitn/notimestamp/nodiarize`, punctuation on); TP not tested.

🔴 Translation requests without a `language` field, the stock OpenAI SDK default, return a plain en→en transcription instead of a translation. `validate_language` turns a missing language into "en", and `get_generation_prompt` then defaults the target to "en". The prompt therefore asks for an English→English transcription, so German audio is decoded as English. Only a warning that names TranscriptionRequest is logged. Fix: for `task_type == "translate"`, reject the request with a 400 when the source language was not supplied or equals the target, while still allowing the transcription default of "en".

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A client calls `/v1/audio/translations` with German audio and no `language`. This is the stock OpenAI `client.audio.translations.create`, which has no language parameter. In serving.py:269 the request goes through `CanaryForConditionalGeneration.validate_language(None)` (canary.py:457-463), which logs a warning and returns "en". In `get_generation_prompt` (canary.py:492-497) the source is "en", and because `to_language` is None the target also becomes "en". The decoder prompt is therefore `<|en|><|en|>`, an English ASR prompt. The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with the audio forced through English transcription, not an English translation. No error tells the client to supply `language`. Nothing in the code guards against this: Canary sets no `supports_explicit_language_detection`, so serving.py:286 never auto-detects the language. The `get_generation_prompt` check at canary.py:493 cannot fire because the language was already defaulted.

**Verification:** In base/serving.py:269, Canary's `validate_language` (canary.py:457-463) sets a missing `language` to "en". For task_type "translate", canary.py:497 sets `target_language = stt_params.to_language or "en"`, which is also "en". The decoder prompt built at canary.py:505 therefore has `<|en|><|en|>`. The request returns 200 with wrong text, and the only signal is a server-side warning.

</details>

+class CanaryPositionalEmbedding(nn.Module):
+    """Fixed sinusoidal table laid out as ``[sin | cos]`` and scaled by
+    ``1 / sqrt(hidden_size)``; matches ``CanaryPositionalEmbedding`` in
+    Transformers."""
+
+    def __init__(self, max_positions: int, hidden_size: int) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        half = hidden_size // 2
+        log_timescale_increment = math.log(10000.0) * 2 / hidden_size
+        inv_timescales = torch.exp(
+            -log_timescale_increment * torch.arange(half).float()
+        )
+        scaled_time = torch.arange(max_positions).float()[:, None] * inv_timescales
+        pos_emb = torch.cat([torch.sin(scaled_time), torch.cos(scaled_time)], dim=1)
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "pos_emb", pos_emb / math.sqrt(hidden_size), persistent=False
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, positions: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.pos_emb[positions]
+
+
+class CanaryDecoderLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config.decoder_config
+        cache_config = vllm_config.cache_config
+        quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+        hidden_size = config.hidden_size
+
+        self.input_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.self_attn = CohereASRAttention(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            num_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
+            bias=config.attention_bias,
+            attn_type=AttentionType.DECODER,
+            cache_config=cache_config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.self_attn",
+        )
+        self.post_attention_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.encoder_attn = CohereASRCrossAttention(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            num_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
+            bias=config.attention_bias,
+            cache_config=cache_config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.encoder_attn",
+        )
+        self.final_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.mlp = CohereASRMLP(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            ffn_dim=config.intermediate_size,
+            act_fn=config.hidden_act,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.mlp",

+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor | None,

🟡 (optional) Translation requests between two non-English languages (for example `language=de`, `to_language=fr`) are accepted, but the model was never trained for them, so output is silently unreliable. In `get_generation_prompt`, a translate task only checks that the target is in `supported_languages`, not that one side is `en`. canary-1b-v2 translates only X→En and En→X. Fix: for `task_type == "translate"`, raise ValueError unless `source_language == "en"` or `target_language == "en"`, the same reject-don't-guess policy `validate_language` uses. Translation from or to English keeps working.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A client calls `/v1/audio/translations` with `language=de` and `to_language=fr`. `serving.py:269-273` runs both values through `CanaryForConditionalGeneration.validate_language`, and both pass because both codes are in `CANARY_SUPPORTED_LANGS`. `get_generation_prompt` (canary.py:496-503) then builds the prompt `<|de|><|fr|>` without checking the pair. The model card for nvidia/canary-1b-v2 lists only English→24 languages and 24 languages→English translation. A non-English pair is outside training, so the request returns HTTP 200 with low-quality or empty text instead of a 400. The PR description says `validate_language` was made strict because an untrained language token made the model silently return empty text (the `ja` case). The pair check leaves that same failure mode open for translation.

**Verification:** Trigger: a translation request where neither side is English (e.g. `language=de`, `to_language=fr`). In `get_generation_prompt` (canary.py ~491-503), the translate branch only checks `target_language not in cls.supported_languages`. Nothing checks whether either side is `en`. `supports_transcription_only = True` does not block this. The request is accepted silently and returns output of unknown quality.

</details>

detail.body:
## Overview

Adds `CanaryForConditionalGeneration` for [`nvidia/canary-1b-v2`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/canary-1b-v2) (FastConformer encoder + Transformer decoder; 25 European languages, ASR + X↔En speech translation). It targets the native Transformers checkpoint layout (`model_type: canary`, available since Transformers 5.16, which vLLM already pins), so no `.nemo` conversion or `trust_remote_code` is needed.

A user asked on the vLLM Slack whether `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` could work. No existing issue or PR: `gh pr list --search canary` / `gh issue list --search canary` only return unrelated NIXL "import canary" CI items.

The decoder is built from vLLM layers; the FastConformer encoder reuses the Transformers module, as `parakeet.py` already does (see Details).

## Claims

- `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` loads and serves via `LLM` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions` + `/v1/audio/translations` (source language from `language`, target from `to_language`, default `en` for translations).
- Greedy output is token-identical to Transformers `CanaryForConditionalGeneration.generate` on the clips below (fp32 and bf16, batched).
- WER on the existing `test_wer_correctness` earnings22 slice: 12.34 (vLLM, bf16, CPU) and 12.336 (vLLM, bf16, L40 GPU, unmodified test) vs 12.46 (Transformers, fp32); 12.34 is added as the expected value for `nvidia/canary-1b-v2`.

## Validation

The runs below are on an Apple M5 Pro (vLLM CPU backend, `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=2`). GPU results are in the next section.

**Token parity vs Transformers** (3 prompts in one `llm.generate` batch, greedy, `max_tokens=128`):

| clip | task | fp32 | bf16 | output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| en (6 s, TTS) | en→en | match | match | `The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Speech recognition on VLLM is now working.` |
| de (5 s, TTS) | de→de | match | match | `Guten Morgen, heute ist das Wetter sehr schön und wir gehen in den Park.` |
| de (5 s, TTS) | de→en | match | match | `Good morning, today is the weather very nice and we go into the park.` |

**WER** (`D4nt3/esb-datasets-earnings22-validation-tiny-filtered`, 511 clips, Whisper `EnglishTextNormalizer`, same code path as `test_wer_correctness`):

| implementation | dtype | WER |

+# ----- Decoder -----
+class CanaryPositionalEmbedding(nn.Module):
+    """Fixed sinusoidal table laid out as ``[sin | cos]`` and scaled by
+    ``1 / sqrt(hidden_size)``; matches ``CanaryPositionalEmbedding`` in
+    Transformers."""
+
+    def __init__(self, max_positions: int, hidden_size: int) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        half = hidden_size // 2
+        log_timescale_increment = math.log(10000.0) * 2 / hidden_size
+        inv_timescales = torch.exp(
+            -log_timescale_increment * torch.arange(half).float()
+        )
+        scaled_time = torch.arange(max_positions).float()[:, None] * inv_timescales
+        pos_emb = torch.cat([torch.sin(scaled_time), torch.cos(scaled_time)], dim=1)
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "pos_emb", pos_emb / math.sqrt(hidden_size), persistent=False
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, positions: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.pos_emb[positions]
+
+
+class CanaryDecoderLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config.decoder_config
+        cache_config = vllm_config.cache_config
+        quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+        hidden_size = config.hidden_size
+
+        self.input_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.self_attn = CohereASRAttention(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            num_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
+            bias=config.attention_bias,
+            attn_type=AttentionType.DECODER,
+            cache_config=cache_config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.self_attn",
+        )
+        self.post_attention_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.encoder_attn = CohereASRCrossAttention(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            num_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
+            bias=config.attention_bias,
+            cache_config=cache_config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.encoder_attn",
+        )
+        self.final_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.mlp = CohereASRMLP(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            ffn_dim=config.intermediate_size,
+            act_fn=config.hidden_act,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.mlp",
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor | None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        residual = hidden_states
+        hidden_states = self.input_layernorm(hidden_states)
+        hidden_states = residual + self.self_attn(hidden_states=hidden_states)
+
+        residual = hidden_states
+        hidden_states = self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states)
+        hidden_states = residual + self.encoder_attn(
+            hidden_states=hidden_states,
+            encoder_hidden_states=encoder_hidden_states,
+        )
+
+        residual = hidden_states
+        hidden_states = self.final_layernorm(hidden_states)
+        hidden_states = residual + self.mlp(hidden_states)
+        return hidden_states
+

+# ----- Multi-modal processing -----
+def _subsampled_length(num_frames: int, encoder_config) -> int:
+    """Mirror of ``ParakeetEncoder._get_subsampling_output_length``."""
+    kernel_size = encoder_config.subsampling_conv_kernel_size
+    stride = encoder_config.subsampling_conv_stride
+    add_pad = (kernel_size - 1) // 2 * 2 - kernel_size
+    length = num_frames
+    for _ in range(int(math.log2(encoder_config.subsampling_factor))):
+        length = math.floor((length + add_pad) / stride + 1.0)
+    return length

+    def _get_hf_mm_inputs(
+        self,
+        mm_items: MultiModalDataItems,
+        hf_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],

+        hf_inputs = super()._get_hf_mm_inputs(mm_items, hf_kwargs)
+        feature_extractor = self.info.get_feature_extractor(**hf_kwargs)

+    def _call_hf_processor(
+        self,
+        hf_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        hf_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],

+        # `CanaryProcessor` renames `input_ids` to `decoder_input_ids`, so call
+        # the feature extractor and tokenizer directly instead.
+        feature_extractor = self.info.get_feature_extractor(**hf_kwargs)
+        audios = hf_data.get("audio")
+        if audios is None:
+            result = BatchFeature()
+        else:
+            if not isinstance(audios, list):
+                audios = [audios]
+            # Extract one item at a time so features are never padded to the
+            # longest clip in the batch.
+            input_features = []
+            feature_lengths = []
+            for audio in audios:
+                features = feature_extractor(
+                    audio,
+                    sampling_rate=feature_extractor.sampling_rate,
+                    return_tensors="pt",
+                )
+                input_features.append(features["input_features"][0])
+                feature_lengths.append(features["attention_mask"][0].sum())
+            result = BatchFeature(
+                dict(
+                    input_features=input_features,
+                    feature_lengths=torch.stack(feature_lengths),
+                )
+            )

+    def _get_mm_fields_config(

+        # unlike the base class, do not fall back for other languages.
+        if language not in cls.supported_languages:
+            raise ValueError(

+                f"{list(cls.supported_languages)}."

+    @classmethod
+    def get_decoder_prompt_tokens(
+        cls, source_language: str, target_language: str, punctuation: bool = True
+    ) -> list[str]:
+        """Same token sequence as the checkpoint's ``chat_template.jinja``."""
+        return [
+            "<|startofcontext|>",

+            "<|emo:undefined|>",

+    @classmethod
+    def get_generation_prompt(cls, stt_params: SpeechToTextParams) -> PromptType:
+        source_language = stt_params.language
+        if source_language is None:
+            raise ValueError("Language must be specified for Canary")
+        target_language = source_language
+        if stt_params.task_type == "translate":
+            target_language = stt_params.to_language or "en"
+            if target_language not in cls.supported_languages:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Unsupported target language {target_language!r}; expected "
+                    f"one of {list(cls.supported_languages)}."

+            # defaults a missing one to "en", so a translation without

+        elif is_list_of(input_features, torch.Tensor):

+            )
+        padded = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_sequence(
+            [f.to(self.dtype) for f in features], batch_first=True, padding_value=0.0
+        )
+        return self.model.get_encoder_outputs(padded, feature_lengths.reshape(-1))
+
+    def compute_logits(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.logits_processor(self.proj_out, hidden_states, self.proj_out.bias)
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        stacked_params_mapping = [
+            # (param_name, shard_name, shard_id)
+            (".self_attn.qkv_proj", ".self_attn.q_proj", "q"),
+            (".self_attn.qkv_proj", ".self_attn.k_proj", "k"),
+            (".self_attn.qkv_proj", ".self_attn.v_proj", "v"),
+            (".encoder_attn.kv_proj", ".encoder_attn.k_proj", "k"),
+            (".encoder_attn.kv_proj", ".encoder_attn.v_proj", "v"),
+        ]
+        params_dict = dict(self.named_parameters())
+        params_dict.update(self.named_buffers())
+        loaded_params: set[str] = set()
+
+        for name, loaded_weight in self.hf_to_vllm_mapper.apply(weights):
+            # The encoder is the Transformers module and keeps unfused q/k/v.
+            is_decoder = name.startswith("model.decoder.")
+            for param_name, shard_name, shard_id in stacked_params_mapping:
+                if not is_decoder or shard_name not in name:
+                    continue
+                name = name.replace(shard_name, param_name)
+                param = params_dict[name]
+                param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id)

+                weight_loader = getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)
+                weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
+            loaded_params.add(name)
+        return loaded_params

inline_comments.body: Let's remove these tests, they aren't really that helpful

🔴 Translation requests without a `language` field, the stock OpenAI SDK default, return a plain en→en transcription instead of a translation. `validate_language` turns a missing language into "en", and `get_generation_prompt` then defaults the target to "en". The prompt therefore asks for an English→English transcription, so German audio is decoded as English. Only a warning that names TranscriptionRequest is logged. Fix: for `task_type == "translate"`, reject the request with a 400 when the source language was not supplied or equals the target, while still allowing the transcription default of "en".

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A client calls `/v1/audio/translations` with German audio and no `language`. This is the stock OpenAI `client.audio.translations.create`, which has no language parameter. In serving.py:269 the request goes through `CanaryForConditionalGeneration.validate_language(None)` (canary.py:457-463), which logs a warning and returns "en". In `get_generation_prompt` (canary.py:492-497) the source is "en", and because `to_language` is None the target also becomes "en". The decoder prompt is therefore `<|en|><|en|>`, an English ASR prompt. The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with the audio forced through English transcription, not an English translation. No error tells the client to supply `language`. Nothing in the code guards against this: Canary sets no `supports_explicit_language_detection`, so serving.py:286 never auto-detects the language. The `get_generation_prompt` check at canary.py:493 cannot fire because the language was already defaulted.

**Verification:** In base/serving.py:269, Canary's `validate_language` (canary.py:457-463) sets a missing `language` to "en". For task_type "translate", canary.py:497 sets `target_language = stt_params.to_language or "en"`, which is also "en". The decoder prompt built at canary.py:505 therefore has `<|en|><|en|>`. The request returns 200 with wrong text, and the only signal is a server-side warning.

</details>

+class CanaryPositionalEmbedding(nn.Module):
+    """Fixed sinusoidal table laid out as ``[sin | cos]`` and scaled by

+    Transformers."""

+    def __init__(self, max_positions: int, hidden_size: int) -> None:

+            -log_timescale_increment * torch.arange(half).float()
+        )

+        pos_emb = torch.cat([torch.sin(scaled_time), torch.cos(scaled_time)], dim=1)
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "pos_emb", pos_emb / math.sqrt(hidden_size), persistent=False
+        )

🟡 (optional) Translation requests between two non-English languages (for example `language=de`, `to_language=fr`) are accepted, but the model was never trained for them, so output is silently unreliable. In `get_generation_prompt`, a translate task only checks that the target is in `supported_languages`, not that one side is `en`. canary-1b-v2 translates only X→En and En→X. Fix: for `task_type == "translate"`, raise ValueError unless `source_language == "en"` or `target_language == "en"`, the same reject-don't-guess policy `validate_language` uses. Translation from or to English keeps working.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A client calls `/v1/audio/translations` with `language=de` and `to_language=fr`. `serving.py:269-273` runs both values through `CanaryForConditionalGeneration.validate_language`, and both pass because both codes are in `CANARY_SUPPORTED_LANGS`. `get_generation_prompt` (canary.py:496-503) then builds the prompt `<|de|><|fr|>` without checking the pair. The model card for nvidia/canary-1b-v2 lists only English→24 languages and 24 languages→English translation. A non-English pair is outside training, so the request returns HTTP 200 with low-quality or empty text instead of a 400. The PR description says `validate_language` was made strict because an untrained language token made the model silently return empty text (the `ja` case). The pair check leaves that same failure mode open for translation.

**Verification:** Trigger: a translation request where neither side is English (e.g. `language=de`, `to_language=fr`). In `get_generation_prompt` (canary.py ~491-503), the translate branch only checks `target_language not in cls.supported_languages`. Nothing checks whether either side is `en`. `supports_transcription_only = True` does not block this. The request is accepted silently and returns output of unknown quality.

</details>

+from .cohere_asr import CohereASRAttention, CohereASRCrossAttention, CohereASRMLP
+from .interfaces import (
+    MultiModalEmbeddings,
+    SupportsMultiModal,
+    SupportsTranscription,
+)
+from .utils import WeightsMapper, make_layers, maybe_prefix
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# See https://huggingface.co/nvidia/canary-1b-v2
+CANARY_SUPPORTED_LANGS = {
+    "bg": "Bulgarian",
+    "hr": "Croatian",
+    "cs": "Czech",
+    "da": "Danish",
+    "nl": "Dutch",
+    "en": "English",
+    "et": "Estonian",
+    "fi": "Finnish",
+    "fr": "French",
+    "de": "German",
+    "el": "Greek",
+    "hu": "Hungarian",
+    "it": "Italian",
+    "lv": "Latvian",
+    "lt": "Lithuanian",
+    "mt": "Maltese",
+    "pl": "Polish",
+    "pt": "Portuguese",
+    "ro": "Romanian",
+    "sk": "Slovak",
+    "sl": "Slovenian",
+    "es": "Spanish",
+    "sv": "Swedish",
+    "ru": "Russian",
+    "uk": "Ukrainian",
+}
+
+
+# ----- Decoder -----
+class CanaryPositionalEmbedding(nn.Module):
+    """Fixed sinusoidal table laid out as ``[sin | cos]`` and scaled by
+    ``1 / sqrt(hidden_size)``; matches ``CanaryPositionalEmbedding`` in
+    Transformers."""
+
+    def __init__(self, max_positions: int, hidden_size: int) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        half = hidden_size // 2
+        log_timescale_increment = math.log(10000.0) * 2 / hidden_size
+        inv_timescales = torch.exp(
+            -log_timescale_increment * torch.arange(half).float()
+        )
+        scaled_time = torch.arange(max_positions).float()[:, None] * inv_timescales
+        pos_emb = torch.cat([torch.sin(scaled_time), torch.cos(scaled_time)], dim=1)
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "pos_emb", pos_emb / math.sqrt(hidden_size), persistent=False
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, positions: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.pos_emb[positions]
+
+
+class CanaryDecoderLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config.decoder_config
+        cache_config = vllm_config.cache_config
+        quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+        hidden_size = config.hidden_size
+
+        self.input_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.self_attn = CohereASRAttention(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            num_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
+            bias=config.attention_bias,
+            attn_type=AttentionType.DECODER,
+            cache_config=cache_config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.self_attn",
+        )
+        self.post_attention_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.encoder_attn = CohereASRCrossAttention(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            num_heads=config.num_attention_heads,
+            bias=config.attention_bias,
+            cache_config=cache_config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.encoder_attn",
+        )
+        self.final_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
+        self.mlp = CohereASRMLP(
+            embed_dim=hidden_size,
+            ffn_dim=config.intermediate_size,
+            act_fn=config.hidden_act,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.mlp",
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor | None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        residual = hidden_states
+        hidden_states = self.input_layernorm(hidden_states)
+        hidden_states = residual + self.self_attn(hidden_states=hidden_states)
+
+        residual = hidden_states
+        hidden_states = self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states)
+        hidden_states = residual + self.encoder_attn(
+            hidden_states=hidden_states,
+            encoder_hidden_states=encoder_hidden_states,
+        )
+
+        residual = hidden_states
+        hidden_states = self.final_layernorm(hidden_states)
+        hidden_states = residual + self.mlp(hidden_states)
+        return hidden_states
+
+
+@support_torch_compile(dynamic_arg_dims={"input_ids": 0, "positions": -1})
+class CanaryDecoder(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config.decoder_config
+        self.hidden_size = config.hidden_size
+
+        self.embed_tokens = VocabParallelEmbedding(
+            config.vocab_size, config.hidden_size
+        )
+        self.pos_emb = CanaryPositionalEmbedding(
+            config.max_position_embeddings, config.hidden_size
+        )
+        self.embedding_layernorm = nn.LayerNorm(config.hidden_size)
+        self.start_layer, self.end_layer, self.layers = make_layers(
+            config.num_hidden_layers,
+            lambda prefix: CanaryDecoderLayer(vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=prefix),
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.layers",
+        )
+        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.hidden_size)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor | None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        hidden_states = self.get_input_embeddings(input_ids, positions)
+        for layer in self.layers:
+            hidden_states = layer(hidden_states, encoder_hidden_states)
+        return self.norm(hidden_states)
+
+    def get_input_embeddings(
+        self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, positions: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        inputs_embeds = self.embed_tokens(input_ids)
+        pos_emb = self.pos_emb(positions).to(inputs_embeds.dtype)
+        return self.embedding_layernorm(inputs_embeds + pos_emb)
+
+
+class CanaryModel(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config: CanaryConfig = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+        # Reuses the Transformers FastConformer encoder as-is, like `parakeet.py`.
+        self.encoder = HFParakeetEncoder(config.encoder_config).to(
+            vllm_config.model_config.dtype
+        )
+        self.decoder = CanaryDecoder(
+            vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "decoder")
+        )
+        assert config.encoder_config.hidden_size == config.decoder_config.hidden_size
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        encoder_outputs: list[torch.Tensor],
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        enc_states = torch.cat(encoder_outputs, dim=0) if encoder_outputs else None
+        return self.decoder(
+            input_ids=input_ids,
+            positions=positions,
+            encoder_hidden_states=enc_states,
+        )
+
+    def get_encoder_outputs(
+        self,
+        input_features: torch.Tensor,
+        feature_lengths: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+        # input_features: (batch, time, num_mel_bins)
+        max_len = input_features.shape[1]
+        attention_mask = (
+            torch.arange(max_len, device=input_features.device)[None, :]
+            < feature_lengths[:, None]
+        )
+        out = self.encoder(
+            input_features=input_features, attention_mask=attention_mask
+        ).last_hidden_state
+        output_lengths = self.encoder._get_subsampling_output_length(feature_lengths)
+        with gpu_sync_allowed():
+            lengths = output_lengths.tolist()
+        return [feat[:length] for feat, length in zip(out, lengths)]
+
+
+# ----- Multi-modal processing -----
+def _subsampled_length(num_frames: int, encoder_config) -> int:
+    """Mirror of ``ParakeetEncoder._get_subsampling_output_length``."""
+    kernel_size = encoder_config.subsampling_conv_kernel_size
+    stride = encoder_config.subsampling_conv_stride
+    add_pad = (kernel_size - 1) // 2 * 2 - kernel_size
+    length = num_frames
+    for _ in range(int(math.log2(encoder_config.subsampling_factor))):
+        length = math.floor((length + add_pad) / stride + 1.0)
+    return length
+
+
+class CanaryProcessingInfo(BaseProcessingInfo):
+    def get_hf_config(self) -> CanaryConfig:
+        return self.ctx.get_hf_config(CanaryConfig)
+
+    def get_default_tok_params(self) -> TokenizeParams:
+        # The decoder prompt is built from control tokens; never add BOS/EOS.
+        return super().get_default_tok_params().with_kwargs(add_special_tokens=False)
+
+    def get_feature_extractor(self, **kwargs: object) -> ParakeetFeatureExtractor:
+        feature_extractor = self.get_hf_processor(**kwargs).feature_extractor
+        assert isinstance(feature_extractor, ParakeetFeatureExtractor)
+        return feature_extractor
+
+    def get_data_parser(self) -> MultiModalDataParser:
+        return MultiModalDataParser(
+            target_sr=self.get_feature_extractor().sampling_rate,
+            target_channels=1,
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def skip_prompt_length_check(self) -> bool:
+        return True  # The encoder prompt is padded
+
+    def get_supported_mm_limits(self) -> Mapping[str, int | None]:
+        return {"audio": 1}
+
+    def get_num_audio_tokens(self, num_samples: int) -> int:
+        fe = self.get_feature_extractor()
+        num_frames = (num_samples + fe.n_fft // 2 * 2 - fe.n_fft) // fe.hop_length
+        return _subsampled_length(num_frames, self.get_hf_config().encoder_config)
+
+
+class CanaryDummyInputsBuilder(BaseDummyInputsBuilder[CanaryProcessingInfo]):
+    def get_dummy_text(self, mm_counts: Mapping[str, int]) -> str:
+        return "<|startofcontext|>" * mm_counts.get("audio", 0)
+
+    def get_dummy_mm_data(
+        self,
+        seq_len: int,
+        mm_counts: Mapping[str, int],
+        mm_options: MultiModalDummyOptions,
+    ) -> MultiModalDataDict:
+        sampling_rate = self.info.get_feature_extractor().sampling_rate
+        audio_len = CanaryForConditionalGeneration.max_audio_clip_s * sampling_rate
+        return {
+            "audio": self._get_dummy_audios(
+                length=audio_len,
+                num_audios=mm_counts.get("audio", 0),
+                overrides=mm_options.get("audio"),
+            )
+        }
+
+
+class CanaryMultiModalProcessor(EncDecMultiModalProcessor[CanaryProcessingInfo]):
+    skip_decoder_start_token: bool = True
+
+    @property
+    def pad_dummy_encoder_prompt(self) -> bool:
+        return True
+
+    def create_encoder_prompt(
+        self,
+        prompt: list[int],
+        mm_items: MultiModalDataItems,
+    ) -> list[int]:
+        # The encoder only consumes audio features; this placeholder is
+        # expanded to the number of encoder output frames.
+        return [0]
+
+    def _get_hf_mm_text(self, mm_counts: Mapping[str, int]) -> str:
+        return self.dummy_inputs.get_dummy_text(mm_counts)
+
+    def _get_hf_mm_inputs(
+        self,
+        mm_items: MultiModalDataItems,
+        hf_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> HFMultiModalInputs:
+        hf_inputs = super()._get_hf_mm_inputs(mm_items, hf_kwargs)
+        feature_extractor = self.info.get_feature_extractor(**hf_kwargs)
+        return hf_inputs._replace(
+            hf_kwargs=dict(
+                hf_inputs.hf_kwargs, sampling_rate=feature_extractor.sampling_rate
+            )
+        )
+
+    def _call_hf_processor(
+        self,
+        hf_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        hf_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> BatchFeature:
+        # `CanaryProcessor` renames `input_ids` to `decoder_input_ids`, so call
+        # the feature extractor and tokenizer directly instead.
+        feature_extractor = self.info.get_feature_extractor(**hf_kwargs)
+        audios = hf_data.get("audio")
+        if audios is None:
+            result = BatchFeature()
+        else:
+            if not isinstance(audios, list):
+                audios = [audios]
+            # Extract one item at a time so features are never padded to the
+            # longest clip in the batch.
+            input_features = []
+            feature_lengths = []
+            for audio in audios:
+                features = feature_extractor(
+                    audio,
+                    sampling_rate=feature_extractor.sampling_rate,
+                    return_tensors="pt",
+                )
+                input_features.append(features["input_features"][0])
+                feature_lengths.append(features["attention_mask"][0].sum())
+            result = BatchFeature(
+                dict(
+                    input_features=input_features,
+                    feature_lengths=torch.stack(feature_lengths),
+                )
+            )
+
+        text = hf_data.get("text")
+        if text is not None:
+            assert isinstance(text, str)
+            token_ids = self.info.get_tokenizer().encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
+            result["input_ids"] = torch.tensor([token_ids])
+        return result
+
+    def _get_mm_fields_config(
+        self,
+        hf_inputs: BatchFeature,
+        hf_processor_mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, MultiModalFieldConfig]:
+        return dict(
+            input_features=MultiModalFieldConfig.batched("audio"),
+            feature_lengths=MultiModalFieldConfig.batched("audio"),
+        )
+
+    def _get_prompt_updates(
+        self,
+        mm_items: MultiModalDataItems,
+        hf_processor_mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+        out_mm_kwargs: MultiModalKwargsItems,
+    ) -> Sequence[PromptUpdate]:
+        def get_replacement(item_idx: int) -> list[int]:
+            audios = mm_items.get_items("audio", AudioProcessorItems)
+            num_samples = audios.get_audio_length(item_idx)
+            return [0] * self.info.get_num_audio_tokens(num_samples)
+
+        return [
+            PromptReplacement(modality="audio", target=[0], replacement=get_replacement)
+        ]
+
+
+@MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.register_processor(
+    CanaryMultiModalProcessor,
+    info=CanaryProcessingInfo,
+    dummy_inputs=CanaryDummyInputsBuilder,
+)
+class CanaryForConditionalGeneration(
+    nn.Module, SupportsTranscription, SupportsMultiModal
+):
+    packed_modules_mapping = {
+        "qkv_proj": ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"],
+        "kv_proj": ["k_proj", "v_proj"],
+    }
+
+    # Only the decoder is built from vLLM layers; encoder weights keep their
+    # Transformers names.
+    hf_to_vllm_mapper = WeightsMapper(
+        orig_to_new_regex={
+            re.compile(r"(decoder\.layers\.\d+\.\w+_attn)\.o_proj\."): (
+                r"\1.out_projection."
+            ),
+            re.compile(r"(decoder\.layers\.\d+\.mlp)\.fc1\."): r"\1.dense_in.",
+            re.compile(r"(decoder\.layers\.\d+\.mlp)\.fc2\."): r"\1.dense_out.",
+            re.compile(r"\.num_batches_tracked$"): None,
+        },
+    )
+
+    supported_languages = CANARY_SUPPORTED_LANGS
+    supports_transcription_only = True
+    skip_warmup_audio_preprocessing = True
+    # TODO: canary-1b-v2 handles long-form audio with dynamic chunking in NeMo;
+    # confirm the right per-chunk limit for vLLM's chunker.
+    max_audio_clip_s: ClassVar[int] = 40
+
+    @classmethod
+    def validate_language(cls, language: str | None) -> str | None:
+        if language is None:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Defaulting to language='en'. If you wish to transcribe audio in "
+                "a different language, pass the `language` field in the "
+                "TranscriptionRequest."
+            )
+            language = "en"
+        # The decoder prompt needs one of the trained language tokens, so
+        # unlike the base class, do not fall back for other languages.
+        if language not in cls.supported_languages:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Unsupported language: {language!r}. Canary supports "
+                f"{list(cls.supported_languages)}."
+            )
+        return language
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_decoder_prompt_tokens(
+        cls, source_language: str, target_language: str, punctuation: bool = True
+    ) -> list[str]:
+        """Same token sequence as the checkpoint's ``chat_template.jinja``."""
+        return [
+            "<|startofcontext|>",
+            "<|startoftranscript|>",
+            "<|emo:undefined|>",
+            f"<|{source_language}|>",
+            f"<|{target_language}|>",
+            "<|pnc|>" if punctuation else "<|nopnc|>",
+            "<|noitn|>",
+            "<|notimestamp|>",
+            "<|nodiarize|>",
+        ]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_generation_prompt(cls, stt_params: SpeechToTextParams) -> PromptType:
+        source_language = stt_params.language
+        if source_language is None:
+            raise ValueError("Language must be specified for Canary")
+        target_language = source_language
+        if stt_params.task_type == "translate":
+            target_language = stt_params.to_language or "en"
+            if target_language not in cls.supported_languages:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Unsupported target language {target_language!r}; expected "
+                    f"one of {list(cls.supported_languages)}."
+                )
+
